results.question: For each user, how many tasks are they assigned? Include users with none.
results.expected_sql:
SELECT u.full_name, COUNT(t.id) AS task_count
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN tasks t ON t.assigned_user_id = u.id
GROUP BY u.id, u.full_name
results.generated_sql:
SELECT u.id, u.full_name, COUNT(t.id) AS task_count
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN tasks t ON t.assigned_user_id = u.id
GROUP BY u.id, u.full_name
ORDER BY u.id
results.raw_output:
{"sql": "SELECT u.id, u.full_name, COUNT(t.id) AS task_count
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN tasks t ON t.assigned_user_id = u.id
GROUP BY u.id, u.full_name
ORDER BY u.id"}

results.question: Show each task's name alongside the name of the workflow it belongs to.

FROM tasks t

results.question: For each blocked task, show the task name, the workflow name and the workflow owner's name.
results.expected_sql:
SELECT t.name AS task_name, w.name AS workflow_name, o.full_name AS owner
FROM tasks t
JOIN workflows w ON w.id = t.workflow_id
JOIN users o ON o.id = w.owner_user_id
WHERE t.status = 'BLOCKED'
results.generated_sql: SELECT t.name AS task_name, w.name AS workflow_name, u.full_name AS workflow_owner_name FROM tasks t JOIN workflows w ON w.id = t.workflow_id JOIN users u ON u.id = w.owner_user_id WHERE t.status = 'BLOCKED' ORDER BY t.id
results.raw_output: {"sql": "SELECT t.name AS task_name, w.name AS workflow_name, u.full_name AS workflow_owner_name FROM tasks t JOIN workflows w ON w.id = t.workflow_id JOIN users u ON u.id = w.owner_user_id WHERE t.status = 'BLOCKED' ORDER BY t.id"}

results.question: Work out how many unfinished tasks each user has, then list the users with more than 2 of them.
results.expected_sql:
WITH open_counts AS (
  SELECT assigned_user_id, COUNT(*) AS open_tasks
  FROM tasks
  WHERE status <> 'COMPLETED' AND assigned_user_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY assigned_user_id
)
SELECT u.full_name, oc.open_tasks
FROM open_counts oc
JOIN users u ON u.id = oc.assigned_user_id
WHERE oc.open_tasks > 2
results.generated_sql:
SELECT u.id, u.full_name, COUNT(t.id) AS unfinished_tasks
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN tasks t ON t.assigned_user_id = u.id AND t.status <> 'COMPLETED'
GROUP BY u.id, u.full_name
HAVING COUNT(t.id) > 2
ORDER BY unfinished_tasks DESC, u.id
results.raw_output:
{"sql": "SELECT u.id, u.full_name, COUNT(t.id) AS unfinished_tasks
FROM users u
LEFT JOIN tasks t ON t.assigned_user_id = u.id AND t.status <> 'COMPLETED'
GROUP BY u.id, u.full_name
HAVING COUNT(t.id) > 2
ORDER BY unfinished_tasks DESC, u.id"}

results.question: Which workflows are healthy, meaning they have no overdue and no blocked tasks?
results.expected_sql:
SELECT w.name
FROM workflows w
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM tasks t
  WHERE t.workflow_id = w.id
    AND (t.status = 'BLOCKED'
         OR (t.due_date < CURRENT_DATE AND t.status <> 'COMPLETED'))
)
results.generated_sql:
SELECT w.id, w.name
FROM workflows w
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM tasks t
    WHERE t.workflow_id = w.id
      AND t.due_date < CURRENT_DATE
      AND t.status <> 'COMPLETED'
)
AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM tasks t
    WHERE t.workflow_id = w.id
      AND t.status = 'BLOCKED'
)
ORDER BY w.id
results.raw_output:
{"sql": "SELECT w.id, w.name
FROM workflows w
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM tasks t
    WHERE t.workflow_id = w.id
      AND t.due_date < CURRENT_DATE
      AND t.status <> 'COMPLETED'
)
AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM tasks t
    WHERE t.workflow_id = w.id
      AND t.status = 'BLOCKED'
)
ORDER BY w.id"}
